parts.note: tolerance in a mechanism is play, a little give
tolerance is also room, space to move

explanation.surface: Patience is on display in the children's nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'Tolerance' supplies both halves: PLAY and ROOM are each a kind of tolerance or leeway.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery is a child's room for games, a straightforward synonym.

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Even a remarkable gift can lie unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exceptional' reads as praise of the talent, but it signals an anagram of TALENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent is present but concealed, not yet showing itself.

clue.text: Make an off-peak call in Switzerland

definitions.text: Make an off-peak call in Switzerland

parts.words: Make an off-peak call in Switzerland
parts.note: an off-peak call sounds like a cheap phone call, but it is a cry made away from the mountain tops in the Alps

explanation.surface: A tip for phoning cheaply while on holiday in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine singers produce this warbling call, sung from slopes below the peaks.

parts.note: going past a mark or target by accident, as a runway or a budget may be passed

explanation.surface: A driver accidentally goes over the speed limit.
explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond a target without meaning to is exactly this verb's sense.

parts.note: the ring suggests boxing, but here it is the bullring and the fighter faces a bull

explanation.surface: Someone who fights in a ring, apparently a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bullfighter performs in the bullring, so the phrase describes him playfully.

parts.note: to bag game is to shoot it
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A hunter asks which island offers good duck shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shoot duck' reads as hunting, but 'duck' is the cricket zero, O.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobago is a Caribbean island, partner of Trinidad.

parts.note: the last of the ten biblical rules, read literally as the final one in the list

explanation.surface: A claim that some rule is the supreme commandment.
explanation.definitionFit: The final commandment of ten is the one numbered last in order.

clue.text: It's not good to make money on a game

parts.note: not good means bad
to mint is to make coins

explanation.surface: Betting on a match is a bad idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Badminton is a racket game played with a shuttlecock over a net.

parts.note: issue means children, so a child of one's own child

explanation.surface: A single question about children.
explanation.definitionFit: A male second-generation descendant is a child born to one's son or daughter.

clue.text: Indigestible food for example …. sent back

indicators.note: sent back means the whole string of letters is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example
the printed dots are read as the word dots

explanation.surface: Complaining that heavy food was returned to the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns the whole run EGDOTS backwards; the row of dots stands for the word DOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food that sits hard in the stomach.

clue.text: Unaware that one has the wrong key?

definitions.text: Unaware that one has the wrong key?

parts.words: Unaware that one has the wrong key?
parts.note: the wrong key suggests a door, but it is a musical key one sings in without noticing

explanation.surface: Someone tries a door with the wrong key and does not realise.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who cannot hear pitch would sing off-key without noticing it.

clue.text: Bound to be stifling in the finish

indicators.note: in places the word for stifling within the word for the finish

parts.note: the finish is the end
stifling weather is close

explanation.surface: Something is sure to be suffocating at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' looks like 'certain', paired with 'to be'; it is the definition, meaning shut in.
explanation.definitionFit: Bound and enclosed both mean fenced or shut in on all sides.

parts.note: a bang sounds like a blow, but bangs are a fringe of hair cut across the forehead

explanation.surface: A knock to the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe, called bangs in America, is one example of a styled haircut.

clue.text: The family's failure makes a wretched story

parts.note: wretched means poor
a relation is an account or story

explanation.surface: A family's black sheep inspires a miserable tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor relation is the less successful member of a family.

clue.text: Presumably he was spotted playing for children

definitions.text: Presumably he was spotted playing for children

parts.words: Presumably he was spotted playing for children
parts.note: spotted reads as seen, but means dressed in patches, the motley piper of Hamelin who led children away

explanation.surface: Someone was noticed performing for kids.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary piper of Hamelin wore pied, multicoloured clothes and lured the town's children away.

clue.text: He might take advantage of a damsel in distress

definitions.text: He might take advantage of a damsel in distress

indicators.note: distress suggests disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A predatory man exploits a woman in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of A DAMSEL IN, signalled by 'distress', gives the answer, while the whole clue describes a womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: A womaniser is the sort who might exploit a vulnerable woman.

parts.note: Haydn's Clock symphony has sections, and the works of a clock are also called by the same name

explanation.surface: A question about a section of Haydn's Clock symphony.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphony is divided into sections, and a clock's mechanism carries the same name.

clue.text: Place for opera company to put on unusually grand event?

indicators.note: unusually signals that the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Somewhere an opera company stages a strange grand occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: COVENT GARDEN is London's Royal Opera House. 'unusually' rearranges GRAND EVENT into VENTGARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Royal Opera House in London is known by its district's name.

definitions.meaning: the house, street and town written on mail

explanation.surface: A speech is scribbled on the back of an envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a formal talk and postal directions share this one word.

definitions.meaning: literally close to a rim or margin

explanation.surface: Someone tense stands close to a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means tense, and literally means positioned at a rim.

clue.text: One addresses one's remarks to him (or her)

definitions.text: One addresses one's remarks to him (or her)

parts.words: One addresses one's remarks to him (or her)
parts.note: addresses sounds like speaking, but means writing an address on letters to a distant correspondent

explanation.surface: Somebody directs comments at a listener.
explanation.definitionFit: A correspondent one writes letters to regularly, often overseas.

clue.text: One taken in by a fat Scottish landowner

parts.note: lard is pig fat
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is fooled by a stout Scottish estate owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird owns a landed estate in Scotland.

clue.text: Vinegar and oil is bound to help the wound

definitions.meaning: a bandage tied on an injury

explanation.surface: Vinegar and oil are sure to heal a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad sauce and a bandage for an injury share this word.

parts.note: sounds like a cheerful face, but means a term relating to the sun

explanation.surface: A cheerful smile.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the sun, an expression about it.

clue.text: Need one tap repaired when the flow is minimal

indicators.note: repaired means put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A plumber is needed to fix a dripping tap.
explanation.definitionFit: A neap tide has the smallest range between high and low water.

indicators.note: in puts the young man inside the spring month

parts.note: May is a spring month
a youth is a lad

explanation.surface: A young person's grumble in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness or ailment.

indicators.note: sorted out suggests reorganising, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Things organised and tidied away.
explanation.definitionFit: Stored means kept somewhere for later, put aside.

parts.note: gates are entries, ways in

explanation.surface: Guards watch over the southern gates.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentries are soldiers posted on watch to protect a place.
